speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin our evaluation, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and have there been any episodes of blood in your stool or unexplained weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infectious Colitis (likely Shigellosis or Campylobacter) leading to Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS-D) sequelae.

I am sorry to hear about your camping trip and the illness affecting your companion; given the duration of four months and the specific symptom of relief with defecation, this suggests an infectious trigger that has evolved into a chronic functional disorder. To confirm if there is an active infection or if this is purely post-infectious, I need to see the results of a Stool Culture and Ova and Parasite exam. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture_AND_Ova_Par
